title: Crispy Mushroom Focaccia
changes_from_base: Cold overnight rise; topped with pre-roasted chestnut and shiitake mushrooms and a little cheese, finished with lemon zest and chives.
summary: A deeply bubbly, cold-risen focaccia covered with crisp roasted mushrooms and finished with lemon zest and chives.
equipment: cling film or a clean tea towel

ingredients.item: shiitake mushrooms, stems removed, caps torn
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Dough
steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast, salt, warm water and 2 tbsp oil to a sticky dough with no dry flour. Rest 15 min, fold it over itself four times round the bowl, then cover and refrigerate 12-24 h. A long cold rise gives big bubbles and a deeper flavour.

steps.title: Tin
steps.text: Oil the tin with 3 tbsp oil, tip in the cold dough and turn it over. Cover and leave in a warm spot 2-3 h, until it has spread out, doubled and wobbles when you shake the tin; ease it into the corners as it softens.

steps.title: Mushrooms
steps.text: Heat the oven to 220 °C (200 °C fan). Toss the mushrooms with 3 tbsp oil, salt and pepper on the roasting tray in one layer and roast 20-25 min, turning once, until browned and shrunken. Driving off their water first means they crisp on the bread instead of making it soggy.

steps.title: Top
steps.text: Dimple the dough deeply, spread the roasted mushrooms over the top and sprinkle with the cheese.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake 25-30 min, until the edges of the mushrooms are crisp and the base is golden; the centre reads about 96 °C.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Scatter the lemon zest and chives over the warm bread, cool 10 min on a rack and cut into 12.

tips: Roast the mushrooms in a single layer; crowded mushrooms steam.
The cold dough is ready to bake when it wobbles like jelly and bubbles show on top.
Add the lemon zest and chives after baking so they stay fresh and bright.
storage: Keep in the fridge for up to 2 days and reheat at 200 °C for 6-8 min until hot through; freeze for up to 1 month. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
